name: Ferrari Testarossa
description:
The Ferrari Testarossa (Type F110) is one of the most iconic and instantly recognizable supercars ever created. Introduced in 1984 as the successor to the Ferrari Berlinetta Boxer, the Testarossa became a defining symbol of 1980s excess and automotive design, with its distinctive side strakes, wide rear track, and dramatic Pininfarina styling making it unmistakable from any angle.

The Testarossa name pays homage to the legendary 1957 Ferrari 250 Testa Rossa sports racing car. 'Testa Rossa' literally means 'red head' in Italian, referring to the red-painted cam covers that adorned both cars' 12-cylinder engines—a visual signature of Ferrari's most exotic powerplants.

At the heart of the Testarossa sits a mid-mounted 4.9-liter flat-12 engine (180-degree V12 configuration) producing 385 horsepower at 6,300 rpm and 490 Nm of torque at 4,500 rpm. This naturally aspirated masterpiece featured four valves per cylinder, Bosch K-Jetronic fuel injection, and Ferrari's traditional 'boxer' layout that kept the engine's center of gravity low. Power was delivered through a 5-speed manual transmission to the rear wheels.

The car's most distinctive feature was its dramatic side strakes—functional cooling vents that channeled air to the radiators mounted alongside the rear-mounted flat-12 engine. This unusual radiator placement necessitated the car's considerable width, making it one of the widest production cars of its era at nearly 2 meters across.

With a top speed of 290 km/h and 0-100 km/h acceleration in approximately 5.7 seconds, the Testarossa offered genuine supercar performance wrapped in one of the most dramatic body styles ever to emerge from Maranello. Produced from 1984 to 1991, with evolutionary successors 512 TR and F512 M following through 1996, the Testarossa remains an automotive icon that defined an entire decade.
author: PedroBLR / RealSpecs
